Image 1 is the turnaround sheet of ONE character, the protagonist of "Cité du Tournoi" (HD-2D pixel art, a sword tournament). Its third figure is his SIDE view, facing LEFT. Image 2 shows the SAME character; its bottom row is his side-view run. Make a NEW sheet of the SAME character FIGHTING WITH A SWORD, every figure in that same SIDE view, FACING LEFT (his face, chest and sword point toward the left edge of the image), as in the third figure of image 1.

Keep his design, colours, proportions and pixel-art rendering exactly as in image 1: brown spiky hair; plain indigo hooded cloak with a thin gold edge and NO motif on the hem; brass clasp; ecru shirt; brown leather vest, belt, pouches and gauntlets; dark grey-brown trousers; tall brown boots with turned-down cuffs. The head, hair included, stays about one third of his standing height. Every figure at the SAME scale as the idle figures of image 1 (a standing figure about 290 pixels tall in this 1536 x 1024 image).

NEW: his sword, the same in every figure: a plain straight one-handed arming sword, a bright steel blade with a darker edge line, about as long as his legs (blade alone about 120 pixels at this scale), a simple brass crossguard and a round brass pommel matching his brass buckles, a short brown leather grip. He holds it in his NEAR hand (the hand closest to the viewer), gauntlet closed around the grip. No scabbard, no shield.

TWO rows. Row 1 has FIVE figures, row 2 has FOUR, in this order, left to right:
Row 1:
1. IDLE: standing at ease, relaxed, feet a little apart, the sword held low in front of him, its point down toward the ground ahead of his feet.
2. READY: combat stance, knees bent, front foot forward and back foot behind, the sword raised forward at chest height, point aimed ahead at an opponent on the left.
3. STRIKE, WIND-UP: the same stance, weight on the back foot, the sword drawn back above his near shoulder, the blade pointing up and behind him.
4. STRIKE, THE CUT: a quick lunge to the left, front knee bent, the sword arm fully extended forward, the blade horizontal at shoulder height pointing left, mouth open.
5. STRIKE, FOLLOW-THROUGH: still lunging, the sword swung down and forward, its point low in front of him.
Row 2:
6. GUARD: feet planted, leaning slightly back, the sword held upright in front of his face and chest to block, the far gauntlet pressed against the flat of the blade.
7. HIT: struck by a blow, recoiling backward to the right, head thrown back, eyes shut, mouth open, the sword arm flung out, the cloak swinging.
8. HIT, RECOVERY: straightening up again, still leaning back a little, the sword coming back in front of him.
9. STUNNED: dazed and out of breath, bent forward, head lowered, shoulders slumped, the sword hanging with its point resting on the ground in front of his feet.

Composition: the feet of every figure of a row on one common ground line; plenty of empty space between the figures (blades included) so they never touch or overlap; nothing cut by the image edge. No motion trails, no speed lines, no sparks, no glow, no effects of any kind: only the character and his sword.

Technique: premium illustrative pixel art, crisp square pixels of one uniform size across the whole sheet (the same pixel size as image 1), controlled colour ramps, selective dark outlines; no blur, no anti-aliasing to the background, no mixed pixel sizes, no dithering, no scattered noise. Plain, flat, uniform neutral grey background like image 1, WITHOUT any cast shadow or floor; no text, labels, numbers, frames, UI or watermark.
